prize_parts.citation: For establishing biomolecular phase separation as a physical-chemical principle that organizes the interior of living cells

statement.case_for: Biomolecular condensation reduces a large, messy part of cell organisation to phase behaviour: demixing, multivalency, interfacial tension and the thermodynamics of weak interactions. Hyman and Brangwynne's 2009 P-granule work gave the concept and Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase diagrams gave the quantitative molecular grammar. More than fifteen years of independent work in RNA biology, neurodegeneration and synthetic biology confirm that the idea is generative, and it brings physical chemistry directly into the chemistry of life. That is a concept-level contribution rather than a tool or a single method.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the physical interpretation of specific in-cell condensates is still contested: how far they are true equilibrium liquid phases, how well they are distinguished from other assemblies, and what their function in vivo is. The three-name limit also leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-encoded grammar and IDR physics are central to the chemistry. A committee wanting a settled molecular mechanism and cleanly bounded credit could reasonably prefer a candidate with a clearer causal chain.

responses.point: Heiner ranks phase separation first as a physical idea with a clear underlying principle (thermodynamics of demixing), original and easy to explain, with the core mature enough despite debate over in vivo condensates.
responses.response: I agree on the principle and on the maturity of the core, but I would not wave away the in vivo debate. Our citation should say phase separation is a physical-chemical principle of organisation and should not claim that every cellular condensate is a liquid. I also want to test the credit split. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen cover the observation and the quantitative framework, but dropping Pappu and Mittag is a real cost, and I do not think the principle is as cleanly attributable as Heiner implies.

responses.point: Daniel puts targeted protein degradation first as a designable chemical modality that changed what chemists and clinicians can do, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core, while granting that no PROTAC has yet been approved.
responses.response: I take the point that B036 is a new capability with a clear chemical principle, and I rank it next. My disagreement is about the type of contribution. Degraders are a modality, and it is still open whether the prize should honour PROTACs or molecular glues. That strand split (Crews and Deshaies versus Handa) means the achievement could be cited as two parts, and either way it leaves out Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto. Phase separation is the single concept that changed how a whole field explains cell organisation. I would like Daniel to say whether he sees a PROTAC-only or a glue-inclusive citation as the cleaner one.

responses.point: Johan puts energy landscape and funnel theory first because it turned folding into a quantitative physical-chemical framework tested by experiment (Fersht), and he regards recognition as overdue.
responses.response: I share the physical-chemical appeal and I list B023 as an alternative. My concern is the 2024 prize on structure prediction and design, which makes the appetite for another protein-folding prize uncertain, and the funnel picture is now mostly background to how people think rather than a recent organising discovery. Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht are also hard to separate from Wolynes and Onuchic. I would like to hear from Johan why he thinks folding is not overshadowed by 2024.

responses.point: Peter ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first as the biological chemistry that most clearly gets stated in physical terms, with Gray and Winkler as a clean two-person pair and decades of confirmation.
responses.response: B067 has the cleanest attribution of any candidate and I respect the physical rigour, which is close to my own standard. I would still place it below B014 because Marcus theory and the tunnelling-pathway theory carry much of the conceptual weight and sit outside the Gray-Winkler pair, so the prize would honour a measurement programme more than the founding concept. I do not see this as a reason to exclude it, and it could pair with another achievement in a two-part prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept that the in vivo debate on condensates does not undermine the core physical-chemical principle.
Whether a three-person cut (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) can be justified when Pappu and Mittag also contributed to the molecular grammar.
Whether a two-part prize pairing phase separation with targeted degradation would be stronger than either alone, given both are concept-driven but only the first is a physical-chemical principle.
How much the 2024 protein structure prize and the 2023 Medicine mRNA prize reduce appetite for B023 and for lipid nanoparticles.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for B014 from the provided profile. As a Lund physical chemist who works on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly in amyloid, I have intellectual proximity to condensate and lipid-nanoparticle science, which is not a personal tie to any named candidate. I am on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and I will watch that this does not substitute for independent judgement.
